established_findings.statement: LLMs can translate natural-language operator intent into concrete network configuration artifacts (e.g., JSON/NSD) in controlled evaluations and testbeds.
limitations: Evaluations are on curated testbeds or focused use-cases (NFV, NSD) rather than broad production networks.
Performance depends on model tuning, prompt strategy, and verification/templates used in those studies.

established_findings.statement: LLM-based agentic workflows and multi-agent systems can automate troubleshooting and incident-diagnosis workflows, showing improvements in success rates or time-to-root-cause in specific deployments/evaluations.
limitations: Reported gains are for particular datasets, incident collections, or operator environments and may not generalize across all NetOps contexts.
Some systems rely on specific model/provider integrations (e.g., proprietary models) reported in the papers.

established_findings.statement: Integrating LLMs into generate–validate–repair pipelines that use formal verification or digital-twin validation reduces unsafe fixes; LLMs used alone often introduce regressions and degrade at larger scales.
limitations: Benchmarks (e.g., Cornetto) are synthetic or semi-synthetic and reflect the benchmark generation choices of the authors.
Verification/digital-twin integration can be computationally expensive and is typically evaluated offline in these works.

established_findings.statement: Agentic (tool-augmented, multi-step) architectures outperform base LLMs on configuration-repair tasks in published evaluations (reported improvements on repair efficacy and safety).
limitations: Reported numeric improvements are specific to the evaluated models, toolchains, and datasets.
Model selection, tuning, and task scope constrain external validity.

established_findings.statement: Formal verification techniques and network digital-twins are used as validators to assess functional correctness of generated or repaired network configurations in recent work.
limitations: Verification is typically applied offline or in iterative closed-loop evaluation rather than as lightweight, always-on production validators in the cited works.
Scalability and latency trade-offs for integrating verification into real-time pipelines remain unresolved in these records.

established_findings.statement: Survey and review literature on LLMs/AIOps/agentic AI for networking highlight hallucination risks, safety challenges, and the need for guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and human-in-the-loop designs.
limitations: Surveys synthesize prior work and identify gaps but do not provide new experimental evidence.
Recommendations vary in specificity and are often high-level.

unresolved_questions.statement: How reliably do LLM-driven repair and configuration systems perform at production scale across heterogeneous topologies, device vendors, and live traffic conditions?
limitations: Cornetto documents performance degradation at scale in benchmarked scenarios but does not provide exhaustive production deployment results across all vendor ecosystems.
Absence of broad production-scale evidence in the supplied records; the question remains open.

unresolved_questions.statement: Which agentic orchestration patterns, human-in-the-loop escalation points, and guardrail designs yield acceptable operational risk/benefit trade-offs for NetOps automation?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: architectural proposals and deployment case studies
limitations: Existing works propose architectures (Aether, StepFly, BiAn) and report case results, but comparative studies of orchestration patterns and human–agent escalation policies are not conclusive in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent can hallucination-detection and self-verification methods reliably prevent unsafe or functionally incorrect NetOps outputs in adversarial or out-of-distribution scenarios?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: method / survey papers addressing hallucination detection and constrained workflows
limitations: Detection and mitigation methods exist but their robustness under adversarial prompt injection and distribution shift is not settled in the provided records.
Some referenced detection frameworks are general-purpose and not NetOps-specific.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a need for standardized, broadly representative benchmarks that measure functional correctness (via formal verification or digital-twin validation) across diverse real-world topologies, vendor configurations, and protocols.
limitations: Cornetto is a step toward such benchmarking but the supplied records indicate further diversity and real-world coverage are still needed.
Building and validating such benchmarks is resource-intensive.

candidate_gaps.statement: Scalable, low-latency integration patterns for formal verification or digital-twin validation into live change-control pipelines are under-explored.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: system/implementation limitations noted in methodological work
limitations: Papers document verification use but emphasize offline or iterative validation; real-time integration trade-offs are not fully resolved in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical studies quantifying operator trust, workload, and decision-quality when interacting with LLM-driven NetOps agents (including controlled HCI measurements) are limited in the supplied literature.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: deployment/case-study papers with limited operator-study content
limitations: Some systems report operational benefits (e.g., reduced MTTR) but rigorous, multi-site HCI studies measuring trust and approval workflows are not evident in the supplied records.

excluded_claims: LLMs are production-ready for fully autonomous, unsupervised NetOps without human oversight (unsupported by the supplied records).
LLM-generated network configurations never introduce regressions or safety faults (contradicted by benchmark findings in Cornetto).
There is conclusive evidence that LLMs universally outperform human operators across all NetOps configuration and repair tasks (unsupported by supplied evaluations).
No verification or tool-augmentation is needed to safely deploy LLMs for network configuration repair (contradicted by multiple papers recommending verification and tool integration).
